direction: T71.7: Re-run T38a dwarf KiSS-SIDM at N=5e4 with extended timeout (3600s -> 7200s) via KISS_SIDM_TIMEOUT_S env var. Goal: complete the dwarf simulation that T38a (2026-08-22) killed at 1 hour.
verdict: TIMEOUT: KiSS-SIDM UFD N=5e4 dwarf hit 7200s wrapper timeout. Even with extended timeout (2x the original 3600s budget), the dwarf simulation cannot complete 10 snapshots within a single chat-session wall-clock budget.
exit_reason: subprocess.TimeoutExpired: Command '['/home/lamkuenai/.juliaup/bin/julia', '+1.11.5', '--project=/home/lamkuenai/KiSS-SIDM', '/tmp/kiss_sidm_worker.jl']' timed out after 7200 seconds

observed_during_run.process_state: Julia subprocess at 99.9% CPU throughout, RAM grew from 1 GB to 3.48 GB
observed_during_run.snapshot_cadence_observed: First 2 snapshots in first ~2 minutes, then NO new snapshots for the remaining ~118 minutes (1 hr 58 min)
observed_during_run.snapshot_directory_post_run: /tmp/kiss_sidm_output/ no longer exists (wiped after timeout; intermediate HDF5 files lost)

interpretation: The wrapper timeout patch (commit cdb9028) WORKED correctly — KISS_SIDM_TIMEOUT_S=7200 was honored and the simulation ran for the full 2 hours. Julia did NOT crash. The simulation simply requires more than 2 hours of wall-clock at N=5e4 dwarf to produce a meaningful r_core/r_s result (likely needs 5+ hours or N=1e4). This is consistent with the T38a partial-finding observation (12 min for 2 snapshots, then 1 hr total for no further progress). The wrapper-level 3600s timeout was NOT the bottleneck — the simulation is structurally compute-prohibitive at UFD scales within a single chat session.

comparison_to_t38a.verdict: Doubling the wall-time budget did NOT proportionally increase the number of completed snapshots. The dwarf KiSS-SIDM simulation has a fundamental wall-time floor that exceeds 7200s for the production N=5e4 dwarf configuration.

options_for_future_work: Option A: N=1e4 (canonical halo) — completes in <30 min, but is not UFD
Option B: Reduce snapshot_count to 3-4 — completes in budget, gives less data
Option C: Use a faster timestep or coarser physics — sacrifices fidelity
Option D: Accept that UFD KiSS-SIDM is out-of-session and ship what we have
